title: Saudia Prohibited Items in Baggage and Cabin | Saudia
desc: View the list of Saudia prohibited items not allowed on board or in checked luggage. Stay compliant and travel safely with Saudia today.
h1: Saudia Prohibited Items in Baggage and Cabin | Saudia
html:
Prohibited items

Prohibited items in checked in or carry-on baggage.

The Banned Carriage of Substances Among the Luggage

For your safety and in line with international regulations, some items are prohibited or restricted in both checked and carry-on baggage on Saudia flights. Please review the following guidelines before you travel.

1. General hazardous materials

Items not allowed on Saudia flights

For safety reasons, the following hazardous materials are not permitted on board:

  • Firearms, ammunition, swords, and knives.
  • Explosives, incendiary materials, flammable substances, toxic substances, and compressed gases.

2. Additional security measures

Restrictions for USA, Canada, and EU flights

For flights departing from or arriving in the United States of America, Canada, and European Union countries, security regulations restrict the carriage of the following in hand baggage:

  • All liquids, gels, toothpaste, liquid cosmetics, and perfumes beyond the permitted limits.
  • Cigarette lighters in both hand baggage and checked baggage.

3. China (CAAC) regulations

Items prohibited in checked baggage

According to the Civil Aviation Administration of China (CAAC), the following rules apply. If any prohibited item is found in checked baggage, it will be removed by airport security.

  1. Prohibited items in checked baggage include:
    • Lighters, lithium batteries, spare batteries, and flammable items.
    • Mobile phones, notebooks, backup power supplies, radio-controlled toys, rechargeable items, nail polish, etc.
    • Electronic cigarettes (all kinds).
    • Gold, jewellery, and cash.
    • All food products and beverages.
  2. Allowable items in carry-on baggage:
    • Mobile phones, notebooks, power banks, power packs, radio-controlled toys, nail polish.
    • Maximum of two pieces per passenger.
    • Note: Some countries (e.g., India) prohibit power banks in carry-on baggage.
  3. Prohibited in both checked and carry-on baggage:
    • Flammable items (lighters, matches, compressed gases, etc.).
    • Detonators, electric sticks, and similar devices.

4. Prohibited & restricted goods (Oman Customs Law)

Items prohibited according to Oman Customs

  • Alcohol in restricted quantities
  • Controlled drugs and medicines
  • Cash exceeding OMR 6,000
  • Electric stun devices, batons, cattle prods
  • Counterfeit tobacco
  • Transparent fishing nets, crossbows, spearguns
  • Wireless communication or bugging equipment
  • Telescopic firearm sights
  • All types of weapons
  • CITES-restricted items (ivory, rhino horn)
  • Remote-controlled aircraft/helicopters
  • Electronic cigarettes
  • Toy guns or items resembling weapons
  • Ammunition and explosives
  • Night-vision goggles
  • Fireworks
  • Radioactive equipment
  • Immoral CDs and magazines
  • Laser pointers
  • Military uniforms and camouflage clothing
  • Walking sticks with hidden blades

5. Lithium battery-powered self-balancing devices

Prohibited electric mobility devices

Saudia does not accept lithium battery-powered self-balancing personal transportation devices on any flight.

  • Examples: hoverboards, balance wheels, air wheels, solo wheels.
  • These devices are prohibited as carry-on or checked baggage on all Saudia flights, including connections, as per IATA and Saudia SLB rules.
  • If a guest arrives with one:
    • The device will not be accepted due to lithium battery risk.
    • The guest will still be permitted to travel.
    • Saudia will not ship the device — the guest must arrange alternative shipping.
Note: If such a device is discovered in checked baggage, it will be removed for safety compliance.
